name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Defensive small/mid-cap growth book after an AI-connectivity drawdown: two smaller earnings-backed growth legs (CRDO, HOOD) with freshly reset, tighter dollar-risk stops and 70% of capital in 4% cash until the sector tape stabilises.
reassessment_note: The AI-connectivity leg of the thesis was hit hard. ALAB stopped out at -27.6% on 10-22 and CRDO is at -24.4%, 0.6% from its -25% stop. That stop has stopped being a risk control: it will fire on any down day at the worst point of the move. My searches found no company-specific break for CRDO, such as a guidance cut or lost customer. The last fundamentals I found were FY2026 revenue of about $1.34B, up roughly 3x, with next-quarter guidance of $465-475M. Past ALAB/CRDO drawdowns were sector-wide AI-capex and valuation scares, but I could NOT find a dated October 2026 explanation, and the price snapshots I found disagree with my packet marks, so my research is thin and I am treating the cause as unknown. Because of that, I am not widening risk. I am cutting it: CRDO goes from about 25% of NAV to 15%, with a fresh 20% stop, which caps further loss on the leg at about 3% of NAV. HOOD reports Q3 after the close on 10-27 (company-confirmed), the day after entry. That is a binary event, so I trim it to 15% with an 18% stop. Cash rises to 70% at 4% APY. I am adding no new names because I could not research replacements properly, and a pick from memory would be worse than cash.

positions.thesis: Credo's AEC/SerDes connectivity business was still compounding at the last report I found: FY2026 revenue was about $1.34B, up about 3x, and Q4 rose 157% y/y with next-quarter guidance of $465-475M. The roughly 24% slide since the 9-30 entry looks like a sector de-rating alongside ALAB, not a broken thesis, though I could not confirm an October cause. I am sizing down to 15% from about 25% of NAV, because a stock at 100x+ trailing earnings in a falling AI tape can keep falling. The fresh 20% stop limits further damage to about 3% of NAV, while the leg keeps exposure to a rebound if the connectivity demand story holds.

Robinhood is a growth platform levered to retail trading, crypto and new products, and it is down about 15% from the 9-30 entry. It reports Q3 2026 after the close on 10-27 (company-confirmed date), the first full session after this entry, against a ChartRow consensus of about $0.55 EPS. Holding through the print keeps exposure to the stock's core growth driver. I trim from about 22% of NAV to 15% because an earnings gap can be large in either direction, and the 18% stop bounds a bad print to under 3% of NAV.
